chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Tamattu' (pilgrims' enjoyment), when does it occur? He said:
He performs the Tamattu' as long as he expects that he will reach the people in Mina.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj separately with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a plain near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj)
key_terms.يُدْرِكُ: To reach or catch up with

ai.seo_question: When does the period for performing Tamattu' Hajj end according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundary for the Tamattu' Hajj, linking the validity of the Umrah Ihram to the pilgrim's reasonable expectation of reaching Mina with the main caravan. This 'reasonableness' standard (*zann*) reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) while maintaining the structural integrity of the two separate Hajj rites. It underscores the importance of intention and timing in distinguishing Tamattu' from Qiran or Ifrad.
